ECE 6390

Eye diagrams and timing margin

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows many received two-symbol slices overlaid for rolloffs 0.25 and 1, with the worst-case vertical opening a quarter symbol after the ideal sampling instant.

An eye diagram overlays short slices of the received waveform, each aligned to the symbol clock. With a raised-cosine combined response g(t) and binary symbols aₙ = ±1, the received signal is y(t) = Σ aₙ g(t − nT). At the ideal instant every neighbor contributes g(kT) = 0, so all traces pass through ±1: zero intersymbol interference.

Away from that instant the neighbor tails no longer vanish. The worst neighbor pattern chooses each sign to oppose the desired symbol, giving the worst-case half-opening h(τ) = g(τ) − Σₖ≠₀ |g(τ − kT)|. The full vertical opening is 2h. When h reaches zero, some symbol pattern crosses the threshold even without noise.

Horizontal width shows timing tolerance; vertical height shows the noise margin left at a chosen sampling time. A larger rolloff α makes g(t) decay faster, so the tails sum to less at an offset. The price is the occupied bandwidth (1 + α)Rs. A finite set of traces samples the possible patterns; the analytic sum bounds all of them.

Noise, filter truncation and channel distortion close the eye further. A receiver samples near the widest opening and tracks that instant, which ties the eye diagram to symbol-timing recovery.

Example

A quarter symbol late, the worst-case half-opening is 0.111 for α = 0.25 and 0.637 for α = 1, compared with 1 at the ideal instant. The wider rolloff keeps more than half of the margin while occupying 2Rs instead of 1.25Rs.

Practice

1. At the ideal sampling instant, how does the eye opening of an ideal raised-cosine response depend on rolloff?

Evaluate g(kT) for nonzero integers k.

It does not depend on rolloff. Every raised-cosine response has g(kT) = 0 for k ≠ 0, so every trace passes through ±1 and the half-opening is 1. Rolloff matters once the sampling instant moves.

2. Why can a short simulated record show a larger opening than the worst-case formula?

Compare the patterns that occurred with every pattern that could occur.

A finite record may never contain the most harmful combination of neighbor signs. The formula gives every tail the opposing sign, so it bounds all patterns; a traced minimum can only be equal or larger.
